context:
Goal: shrink the open-PR pile without losing wanted work (your words at 15:31 CST: bundle them to see if they are still wanted and make sense to land).
Problem (cannot undo): closing the three PRs drops a refusal at merge time that no other PR carries, so it needs your word.
Based on (ruling): your 15:31 CST chat answer: match the PRs to steps, bundle them, and judge each; no PR closes before you see the list.
Based on (ruling): record pr-review-record, question 1, pick a: no refusal at merge time for now.
Based on (measured): a Sonnet reader compared the stack with main at 2d6f67f7c: main's review check already says round 3 is owed after a fix check, and `merge --release-check` holds the gate; only a refusal at merge time is missing; all three conflict with main and sit about 3,000 commits behind.
Departs from: main (the three PRs stay open) — the batch runner closes all three with a note naming the review check and `merge --release-check` on main.
Meanwhile: the other wanted bundles are queued on the roadmap to merge main and land; nothing closes before your answer.
home: step-matching pass for the 281 open PRs that cite no step

lastAnswer.note: is this still a real open question?

options.gain: Three fewer stale PRs, and the round-3 gate stays on main as it is today.
options.how: The batch runner closes #1773, #1939 and #1994 with a note naming what on main covers them; each branch is kept on an archive branch.
options.label: Close all three (Recommended)
options.lose: No refusal at merge time for a missing round 3, which record pr-review-record already chose not to have for now.

options.gain: A refusal at merge time is ready if you want it later.
options.how: A lane merges main into the stack and runs its review again.
options.label: Keep them, merge main in later
options.lose: A lane spends time on a change your earlier pick put aside, and the merge clashes with another open PR that rewrites the same round-3 rules.

reply: No (12:04 CST). Your ruling R9 (Nov 10 15:44 CST: "i never wanted round 3 if it passed earlier") already rules out a merge-time refusal for a missing round 3, which is all these three add. Triage closes #1773, #1939 and #1994 with a note citing R9; each branch is kept, so any of them can reopen.
title: Close #1773, #1939 and #1994, the merge-tool round-3 stack that main already covers?
why: Of the 31 doubtful PRs, this is the only bundle whose change main already covers; the rest still look wanted and need main merged in.
